jobs.title: Managing Director, Teachers' Venture Growth - North America Direct Investing
jobs.description:
The Opportunity

Ontario Teachers’ Pension Plan (“Teachers’”) manages ~C$270B globally and is recognized as one of the most sophisticated direct investors in the world. With over 80% of assets managed internally, we combine long-term capital with disciplined underwriting and the ability to lead at scale. Teachers’ Venture Growth (TVG) is our dedicated late-stage venture and growth equity platform, managing ~C$15B globally. On the direct investment front, we deploy ~C$1B annually into minority investments in scaled private technology companies. TVG has invested in category leaders such as SpaceX, Databricks, Canva, Anthropic, Gusto, Grafana, Kong, StackAdapt, and many others.

We are seeking a Managing Director in San Francisco
to join our North America Direct team. We are intentionally looking to add a Silicon Valley-based investor who brings differentiated access, cycle-tested judgment, and the ambition to help scale a high-performing institutional growth platform.

The Mandate

You Will

Own sector coverage within North American technology
Develop differentiated investment theses
Originate, lead, and close minority growth investments (typically Series C +)
Write and defend investment committee recommendations
Serve as an active board member or observer
Develop junior talent and elevate team performance

TVG’s average initial equity commitment is ~US$100M and we frequently lead or co-lead rounds. You will collaborate closely with senior TVG leadership, the TVG Funds team, and adjacent OTPP asset classes, but investment decisions and portfolio ownership resides within TVG.

What Success Looks Like

Within the first 12–24 months, you will have:

Expanded our access to high-quality companies and founders not already in our network
Led and closed compelling later-stage investments
Demonstrated strong board engagement and value-add through inflection points
Raised the bar for analytical rigor and decision quality across the team
Developed junior investors through direct coaching and meaningful ownership

We are building the next phase of our North America platform and this role is expected to contribute materially to that evolution.

The Profile

We Are Seeking An Investor Who Brings

12+ years of direct investing experience in later-stage venture or growth equity
A demonstrated track record leading minority investments in scaled technology companies
Meaningful board experience and exposure through exit
Deep, credible relationships across Silicon Valley and the broader North American technology ecosystem
Strong transaction leadership and negotiation capabilities

We will not consider candidates whose experience is limited to early-stage investing or those without direct underwriting responsibility.

Equally Important

Experience investing through multiple market cycles with visible evidence of judgment shaped by volatility
High standards, intellectual independence, and accountability
A collaborative, strengths-based leadership style suited to a global institutional platform

We focus primarily on later-stage technology assets across a wide range of sectors, however, we are generally less active in consumer internet and health tech.

Why Teachers’

Teachers’ Offers Something Distinctive In Silicon Valley

Long-duration capital that allows us to invest through cycles
The ability to write large checks and lead
A disciplined, globally integrated investment culture
A truly global platform with deep institutional resources
A clear purpose: delivering retirement security to 340,000 teachers who rely on us for long-term financial stability in retirement

Our capital is not transient. It represents the deferred earnings of educators. That responsibility shapes how we underwrite risk, support companies, and build enduring value. This is an opportunity to combine institutional scale with entrepreneurial impact.

Compensation

Base salary range: USD $300,000–$380,000
, plus eligibility for Teachers’ annual incentive plan and Long Term Incentive Plan compensation programs. Final compensation reflects experience, capability, and internal alignment.

What We’re Offering

Numerous opportunities for professional growth and development
Comprehensive employer paid benefits coverage
A flexible work environment combining in office collaboration and remote working
Competitive time off
Our Flexible Travel Program gives you the option to work abroad in another region/country for up to a month each year

At Ontario Teachers', diversity is one of our core strengths. We take pride in ensuring that the people we hire and the culture we create, reflect and embrace diversity of thought, background and experience. Through our Diversity, Equity and Inclusion strategy and our Employee Resource Groups (ERGs), we celebrate diversity and foster inclusion through events for colleagues to connect for professional development, networking & mentoring. We are building an inclusive and equitable workplace where our talent is respected, accepted and empowered to be themselves. To learn more about our commitment to Diversity, Equity and Inclusion, check out Life at Teachers'.

How To Apply

Are you ready to pursue new challenges and take your career to the next level? Apply today! You may be invited to complete a pre-recorded digital interview as part of your application.

Accommodations are available upon request (peopleandculture@otpp.com) for candidates with a disability taking part in the recruitment process and once hired.

Candidates must be legally entitled to work in the country where this role is located.

Ontario Teachers’ may use AI-based tools to assist in screening and assessing applicants for this position. These tools may help us identify candidates whose skills and experience align with Ontario Teachers’ objectives by analyzing information provided in resumes and applications. Our use of AI does not replace human decision-making.

To learn more about how Teachers’ uses AI with your personal information, please visit our Privacy Centre.

jobs.title: Executive Director, Support Services
jobs.description:
The New York City Department of Sanitation (DSNY)’s primary mission is to keep New York City healthy, safe, and clean. This is accomplished by collecting, recycling, and disposing of waste, cleaning City streets and vacant lots, and removing snow and ice. DSNY is the nation's largest municipal sanitation agency, with nearly 10,000 employees, 59 district garages, and a fleet of more than 5,000 trucks, passenger vehicles, and other operational types of equipment. The Department clears litter, snow, and ice from approximately 6,500 miles of City streets and removes debris from vacant lots as well as abandoned vehicles from City streets.

The Executive Director of the Division of Support Services is responsible for the executive management and strategic oversight of the Offices of Administration, Procurement, and Fiscal Services. Reporting directly to the Assistant Commissioner of Support Services, the Executive Director ensures that all administrative, procurement, fiscal, and operational support functions are performed accurately, efficiently, and in compliance with all applicable New York City laws, oversight requirements, and agency policies. The Executive Director provides leadership in the development and implementation of strategic initiatives that enhance operational effectiveness, strengthen internal controls, and improve service delivery across the Division. The position oversees supervisory personnel, establishes clear expectations and accountability, and promotes continuous improvement through effective policy implementation, system development, and process optimization.

Duties

Working collaboratively with the Office of Vehicle Acquisition and Warranty (VAW), Fleet Operations, Materials Management, and other Support Services units, the Executive Director ensures that operational priorities are supported through effective fiscal planning, procurement, and administrative services. Duties include but are not limited to:

Provide executive leadership and strategic direction for the Offices of Administration, Procurement, and Fiscal Services.
Oversee the Division's Personal Services (PS), Other Than Personal Services (OTPS), and Capital Budgets, ensuring responsible fiscal management and timely execution of expenditures.
Direct all procurement activities, ensuring compliance with New York City Procurement Policy Board (PPB), Mayor's Office of Contract Services (MOCS), and other applicable procurement regulations.
Supervise Accounts Payable operations, ensuring vendor invoices are processed accurately and within Comptroller requirements.
Ensure fiscal resources and procurement support are effectively aligned with Fleet Operations, Vehicle Acquisition and Warranty (VAW), and other operational units.
Manage the allocation of OTPS and Capital funding for vehicle acquisitions, maintenance, repairs, and related operational expenditures.
Develop and implement policies, procedures, and internal controls that promote operational efficiency, accountability, and regulatory compliance.
Lead and mentor supervisory staff while fostering a collaborative, high-performing work environment.
Monitor organizational performance, identify operational improvements, and implement best practices across administrative, fiscal, and procurement functions.
Build and maintain strong working relationships with executive leadership, internal business units, oversight agencies, vendors, and external stakeholders.
Represent the Division in interagency meetings, strategic planning initiatives, and executive-level discussions.

ADMINISTRATIVE STAFF ANALYST - 10026

Minimum Qualifications

A master's degree from an accredited college in economics, finance, accounting, business or public administration, public health, human resources management, management science, operations research, organizational behavior, industrial psychology, statistics, personnel administration, labor relations, psychology, sociology, human resources development, political science, urban studies or a Juris Doctor degree from an accredited law school, and two years of satisfactory full-time professional experience in one or a combination of the following: working with the budget of a large public or private concern in budget administration, accounting, economic or financial administration, or fiscal or economic research; or in management or methods analysis, operations research, organizational research or program evaluation; or in personnel or public administration, recruitment, position classification, personnel relations, labor relations, employee benefits, staff development, employment program planning/administration, labor market research, economic planning, social services program planning/evaluation, or fiscal management. Eighteen (18) months of this experience must have been in an executive, managerial, administrative, or supervisory capacity. Supervision must have included supervising staff performing professional work in the areas described above.
A baccalaureate degree from an accredited college and four years of satisfactory full-time professional experience in the areas described in “1” above, including the 18 months of executive, managerial, administrative, or supervisory experience, as described in “1” above.
An associate degree or completion of 60 semester credits from an accredited college and six years of satisfactory full-time professional experience as described in “1” above, including the 18 months of executive, managerial, administrative, or supervisory experience, as described in “1” above.
A four-year high school diploma or its educational equivalent approved by a State’s department of education or a recognized accrediting organization and eight years of satisfactory full-time professional experience as described in “1” above, including the 18 months of executive, managerial, administrative, or supervisory experience, as described in “1” above.
A combination of education and/or experience equivalent to “1”, “2”, “3”, or “4” above. College education may be substituted for professional experience at the rate of 30 semester credits from an accredited college for one year of experience. However, all candidates must have a high school diploma and at least two years of experience as described in “1” above, including the 18 months of executive, managerial, administrative, or supervisory experience, as described in “1” above.

Preferred Skills

Minimum of five (5) years of progressively responsible management experience in public sector administration, procurement, fiscal management, or related operational leadership. - Extensive knowledge of New York City procurement regulations, including PPB Rules and MOCS requirements. - Strong understanding of OTPS and Capital Budget administration, financial planning, and budget monitoring. - Experience overseeing procurement operations, contract administration, vendor management, and accounts payable functions. - Knowledge of payroll administration, timekeeping, leave administration, workers' compensation, retirement processing, and applicable collective bargaining agreements. - Demonstrated experience in strategic planning, financial analysis, policy development, and implementation of internal controls. - Proven ability to lead multiple operational units while managing competing priorities in a fast-paced environment. - Exceptional leadership, organizational, analytical, and decision-making skills. - Strong project management skills with the ability to lead cross-functional initiatives and organizational change. - Excellent written and verbal communication skills with the ability to effectively engage executive leadership, oversight agencies, vendors, and internal stakeholders. - Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite, particularly Microsoft Excel for financial analysis and reporting. - Experience using New York City financial, procurement, payroll, and personnel management systems. - Demonstrated ability to build collaborative partnerships and foster teamwork across diverse operational and administrative functions.

Salary range is $171k to $325k, with a midpoint of $248k. New hires typically receive between minimum and midpoint, however, we may go slightly higher based on experience, internal equity and market.

Sound Transit also offers a competitive benefits package with a wide range of offerings, including:

Health Benefits: We offer two choices of medical plans, a dental plan, and a vision plan all at no cost for employee coverage; comprehensive benefits for employees and eligible dependents, including a spouse or domestic partner.
Long-Term Disability and Life Insurance.
Employee Assistance Program.
Retirement Plans: 401a – 10% of employee contribution with a 12% match by Sound Transit; 457b – up to IRS maximum (employee only contribution).
Paid Time Off: Employees accrue 25 days of paid time off annually with increases at four, eight and twelve years of service. Employees at the director level and up accrue additional days. We also observe 12 paid holidays and provide up to 2 paid floating holidays and up to 2 paid volunteer days per year.
Parental Leave: 12 weeks of parental leave for new parents.
Pet Insurance.
ORCA Card: All full-time employees will receive an ORCA card at no cost.
Tuition Reimbursement: Sound Transit will pay up to $5,000 annually for approved tuition expenses.
Inclusive Reproductive Health Support Services.
Compensation Practices: We offer competitive salaries based on market rates and internal equity. In addition to compensation and benefits, you’ll find that we provide work-life balance, opportunities for professional development and recognition from your colleagues.

General Purpose

Under general direction of the Chief Planning and Development Officer, leads and administers Sound Transit’s Community Development division, including setting strategic direction for its transit-oriented development (TOD), joint development, community activation and related programs, overseeing the development/disposition of the agency’s excess property portfolio and executing transit oriented, joint development and other real estate transactions using Sound Transit properties.

Essential Functions

The following duties are a representative summary of the primary duties and responsibilities. Incumbent(s) may not be required to perform all duties listed and may be required to perform additional, position-specific duties.

Plans, directs, coordinates, and reviews the staff work of the Community Development Office, including TOD and Joint Development teams, community activation and other efforts; assigns work activities and coordinates schedules, projects, and programs; provides constructive feedback; reviews and evaluates work and makes effective suggestions and recommendations.
Supports the Chief Planning and Development Officer in developing strategic direction for and oversight of the agency’s Community Development workplan; directs the TOD and joint development programs, and property disposition functions to ensure compliance with the agency’s equitable TOD policy along with federal, state, and other ST policies, procedures and guidelines; assumes management responsibility for the services and activities of the Community Development Office.
Ensures active, ongoing coordination with Sound Transit staff on capital delivery projects to maximize TOD and related community development outcomes within ST’s capital program, maintaining strong working relationships with peers across the agency to support advancing TOD and related community development outcomes as projects advance to construction.
Supports local government and other community partners in achieving TOD and related outcomes around ST stations and services throughout the region, leveraging staff and consultant expertise to help ensure local zoning and development regulations support TOD outcomes and by providing create public financing support to help deliver local transit-supportive infrastructure.
Oversees the agency’s community partnerships around TOD and maintains strong working relationships with planning and economic development leaders across the region.
Advances a diverse range of community development projects to realize goals of increased transit ridership, revenue generation, economic development, and vibrant station areas that include a diversity of housing options with a priority to affordability and mix of uses.
Ensures the integration of program priorities into project development at the corridor level; provides technical support and participates in local, regional, and state initiatives to improve land use/transit connectivity.
Provides independent, strategic advice to ST leadership on a range of planning and real estate issues; leverages staff and consultant resources to direct market studies and feasibility analysis; summarizes findings and provides recommendations to the agency’s leadership and Board of Directors.
Oversees the preparation of program reports for executive leadership, the state legislature, agency’s Board of Directors, and external audiences; oversees implementation of the Community Development Office’s TOD Strategy by identifying the development pipeline that best implements agency policies, establishing annual goals and reporting on metrics and outcomes.
Closely coordinates with and provides strategic support for real estate functions, including market capacity, appraisal and acquisition, property or asset management.
Administers and manages consultant assignments in support of the Community Development Office and for a variety of internal clients; participates on Agency or external committees to address initiatives of broader Agency interest.
Negotiates complex real estate and development transactions for property on and adjacent to Sound Transit facilities (stations, auxiliary spaces, guideways, and rails) including obtaining rights needed for long term operations and maintenance of the system.
Champions and models Sound Transit's core values and demonstrates values-based behaviors in everyday interactions across the agency.
Contributes to a culture of diversity, equity and inclusion in alignment with Sound Transit’s Equity & Inclusion Policy.
It is the responsibility of all employees to follow the Agency safety rules, regulations, and procedures pertaining to their assigned duties and responsibilities, which could include systems, operations, and/or other employees.
It is the responsibility of all employees to integrate sustainability into everyday business practices.
Other duties as assigned.

Minimum Qualifications

Education and Experience:
Bachelor’s degree in Urban Planning, Urban Studies, Real Estate, Urban Geography, or closely related field; Ten years of progressive experience managing complex real estate, planning, and TOD projects and programs and other real estate developments, including hands-on expertise with a range of real estate development types, capital projects, right-of-way acquisition, project negotiation, community planning, and building construction.; Or an equivalent combination of education and experience. Eight years of leadership, budgetary, planning and workforce management experience.

Required Knowledge And Skills

Practicing understanding of core principles of urban planning and urban land economics, including development planning, transportation planning and approaches to equitable community engagement.
Operational characteristics, services, and activities of a transit oriented and joint development real estate project transactions, real estate acquisition, relocation, property management, and disposition.
Real estate property principles and practices related to the appraisal, acquisition, management, and sale or lease of public real property assets.
Principles and practices of program development and administration.
Principles and practices of economic development.
Project management techniques and principles.

Jewish Federation of Palm Beach County is a 501(c)3 nonprofit that mobilizes the community to care for those in need, activate Jewish life, safeguard the people of Israel, and combat antisemitism and hatred locally and in more than 70 countries worldwide. Staff play a direct role in advancing this work across the Palm Beaches and beyond.

Position Summary
:
The Director of Managed Campaigns is responsible for managing a diverse donor portfolio, cultivating and soliciting donors and prospects for annual gifts in the $1,000-$10,000+ range. The Director manages the strategy and execution of assigned managed campaigns, which may include local gated communities and other priority segments, to drive increased Annual Campaign results. Reporting to the Vice President, Annual Campaign, the Director of Managed Campaigns manages Development Officer(s) and collaborates closely with colleagues across the organization. Fundraising Strategy and Campaign Management
